ResearcherxB.unlockedByHtml:
Setting up a Triangulation Device on Vindict and another six random moons as prompted. This must be accomplished within a random number of days of in-game time, as ResearcherxB can no longer be located and will begin to crash onto Trite otherwise. This change is permanent on that save file. Players can receive at least three distress signals from the ship while on a moon and each signal warns players of how many days are remaining. Being fired will reset triangulation progress but will not affect the countdown.

Triangulation Devices can be crafted on Galetry or Gratar. Additionally, there is a chance to find a device on the exteriors of Glace, Selector, Trite, and Vindict on caches of scrap that can be collected once per save file. Excluding the "Recovery order", this scrap is randomized per landing and players can reroll what scrap is there by not getting too close to the cache.

health stim.d: Heals 75hp. Overcaps health to 125hp. Has two uses. Recipe: 1 Plastic stock; 1 Chemicals.

airhorn.d: The Airhorn is a weightless, mid-high value Scrap that can be found on almost every Moon. The horn itself is red and blue, with a yellow label for a fictional brand reading “AIRY BLAST”.

ammo.d: Ammo (short for 'ammunition'), a.k.a. Shotgun shell, is a consumable item in the game, exclusively dropped from Nutcrackers. It becomes available for collection after defeating a Nutcracker.

apparatus.d: Sell for ~80, or keep one for the Repress ship repair (needed for every ending). Pulling it cuts the building's power.

bell.d: The Bell (or "Brass bell") is a Scrap item in Lethal Company. It is considered common, appearing on more than half of the game's Moons and is mid-to-high tier in terms of value. It does not have any particular use or possible interactions.

belt bag.d: The Belt bag is a blue fanny pack that can be purchased from the equipment store for , used for carrying multiple equipment items with only a single hotbar slot taken up.

big bolt.d: The Big bolt is a low-value Scrap that's able to spawn on almost every moon. Despite its name, the Big bolt appears to be a screw, not a bolt. As it is made of metal, it can trigger a lightning strike during stormy weather.

binoculars.d: Binoculars are a scrapped equipment item. They can be spawned in with mods but are not functional. There is also a bug involving Gifts where they can contain an item they shouldn't, Binoculars being one of the possibilities.

body.d: A Body is the corpse of a deceased employee, effectively a ragdoll which has inherited their appearance.

bone.d: A weightless body part Scrap exclusive to Dine. The model of this item is reused from [https://store.steampowered.com/app/1717770/The_Upturned/ The Upturned], another game by Zeekerss.

cash register.d: The Cash Register is a Scrap item in Lethal Company. It is considered uncommon, appearing mostly with low chances of on most of the Moons where it spawns, despite there being seven. It is a high tier item in terms of Value, along with Gold bars or Zed Dogs and is the heaviest item in the game.

clipboard.d: The clipboard (a.k.a. Training manual a.k.a. Service manual) is a pedagogical item which generates in the ship and in the Company Cruiser. Both contain multiple pages of gameplay information, interspersed with worldbuilding. They have little use beyond that. The "Training manual" clipboard will always appear to the left of the brake lever upon creating or loading a save, even if moved, left in a Belt bag, or lost.

clown horn.d: Produces a honking sound when used that can be heard by other employees and (some) nearby wildlife. As it is made of metal, it can trigger lightning strikes when placed on the ground or held by an employee during stormy weather.

dust pan.d: The Dust pan is a Scrap item that can only found in Experimentation. Though it weighs nothing, dustpans are very low value, only higher than the lowest values in the game, i.e. metal sheets and whoopie cushions.

easter egg.d: The Easter egg is a small, colorful egg with 5 variants. It can be thrown with , and has a small chance to explode upon hitting the ground. The chances of an Easter egg exploding are the same regardless of whether it's been dropped, thrown, or placed inside of another object such as the Cupboard.

egg.d: thumb|right| A newly-hatched Sapsucker, moments before calling for its mother These are the eggs laid by a mother Sapsucker. Similar to the Circuit bees' nest, they sell for a good price, but come with danger. When an egg has been carried a certain distance from its nest, it will hatch after six seconds to reveal a baby Sapsucker.

egg beater.d: The Egg beater is a low-value Scrap that can be found on Tier 1 Moons as well as Adamance. As it is made of metal, it can trigger lightning strikes when held by an employee or placed on the ground during stormy weather.

extension ladder.d: The Extension Ladder can be used to reach otherwise difficult-to-reach or inaccessible locations. It weighs nothing, making it easy for employees to carry.

flashlight.d: Flashlight Flashlights are tools used to emit light in a conical shape in front of an employee, aiding exploration. Fully charged flashlights last for 140 seconds.

foot.d: Foot A weightless body part Scrap that appears on both Rend and Dine.

gift.d: The Gift is a Scrap item that can be opened to reveal a different, random scrap item inside. The dropped scrap item can be anything that's normally able to spawn on whichever moon the Gift was originally found. The item may be two-handed, despite the Gift being a one-handed scrap item.

gold bar.d: Gold bar The Gold bar is a high-value Scrap item. It is a very rare and heavy scrap item with the highest possible value of any item in the game. Despite its weight only being beaten by Cash registers, it is a one-handed item.

hairdryer.d: Noisemaker: makes a loud sound (10 uses on its battery) that players and sound-hunting enemies hear. Can lure Eyeless Dogs away, but also gives you away. Otherwise sell (~80).

hand.d: Hand A very low-value body part Scrap exclusive to Dine.

heart.d: A rare, high-value body part Scrap exclusive to Dine. Hearts will continuously make a beating sound, which allows them to be heard from a distance and located easier.

homemade flashbang.d: The Homemade Flashbang is similar to the Stun grenade, but its "fuse" is extremely short. Pulling the pin will cause it to explode almost immediately, flashing everything in the vicinity, but also dealing minor damage (20HP) to the employee that was holding it.

jetpack.d: The jetpack is a versatile yet clunky mobility tool used to travel around the surface of the moons. It is both the heaviest and most expensive piece of equipment in the game, but it makes up for this with its incredible aerial mobility. Its near-exclusively vertical thrust and incredible weight make it practically worthless within the interior areas of moons.

key.d: A small golden key. Used to unlock locked doors within interiors or the door to the Cabin on Adamance and is consumed on use. The key is made of metal and can trigger lightning strike on a stormy moon.

kitchen knife.d: The Kitchen Knife is a type of scrap that can also function as weapon for eliminating entities or destroying spider webs. It has a fixed sell value of .

knee.d: Knee The Knee is a body part Scrap exclusive to Dine. It's the only body part item aside from the Heart that weighs more than .

laser pointer.d: The Laser pointer is a mid-to-high-value Scrap that can be powered on like a Flashlight. When turned on, it emits a small orange light beam with an estimated range of 20m and 5 minutes of battery life. Impractical use for navigation, but it can be used as a replacement for Flashlights if you're out of options. The laser dot will be obscured by fog, steam, blizzards, and toxic fumes.

lockpicker.d: Lockpickers are tools used to gain access to locked doors. Upon placing one on a locked door, it remains there for 30 seconds before falling to the ground and unlocking the door. They are not consumed through use allowing them to be used repeatedly.

magic 7 ball.d: Magic 7 ball The Magic 7 ball is a mid-value Scrap. It's a play on the iconic toy series "Magic 8 Ball". Despite its name, it has no magical properties and cannot give answers to questions.

magnifying glass.d: Magnifying glass The Magnifying glass is a mid-value Scrap with translucent blue glass. Despite being an object you'd expect to hold up to your eye, this item is not inspectable in-game.

maneater.d: The Maneater is a deceptively cute indoor entity resembling an insect. While it initially appears to be a sensitive, carriable infant requiring constant care and maintenance, it transforms into a monstrous, extremely fast and deadly enemy if upset or provoked. The moon they are most commonly found on is Vow.

mapper.d: The Mapper (called Mapper tools in the store) is a utility item, which may eventually be purchasable but is currently inaccessible in-game. (A purchase flow exists, but it has the price of the Shovel and will add one of those to the Dropship instead.)

masks (item).d: Masks cannot possess an employee if the employee does not put it on themselves. Dying with a mask in one's inventory or holding it without putting it on does nothing.

mug.d: Mug The Mug (or, "Coffee mug") is a low-to-mid-value Scrap that can spawn in one of 5 different variants.

old phone.d: The Old phone is a mid-value Scrap depicting a black satellite phone. When switching to this item while it is in your inventory, it will play an audio clip: firstly a garbled static sound, followed by someone screaming, and finally a long disconnect tone. This sound can be heard by other players and hearable entities, such as Eyeless Dogs.

pro-flashlight.d: Though Pro-Flashlights only weigh 5 pounds, it is enough to noticeably affect running speed and stamina depletion. For example, when trying to secure Bee Hives, it is advised to leave these flashlights at the ship for an extra few seconds of running.

radar-booster.d: The Radar Booster can be purchased in the Store. When turned on, it can be used as another camera from the terminal. It also appears when an employee scans (right clicks).

remote.d: Turns lights on and off in ship when activated.

shotgun.d: The Shotgun is a scrap item that also functions as a weapon. It does not generate naturally, and is instead only wielded and dropped by Nutcrackers, along with however many shells the Nutcracker had in the shotgun when it died, with 2 extra shells dropped alongside it. It has a fixed sell value of regardless of how many shells are loaded.

shovel.d: The Shovel can be used to eliminate Entities or destroy Bunker Spider webs.

soccer ball.d: A generic-looking Soccer Ball, or football. Only Scrap Item in the game that can be moved without being picked up, as Players and other entities are able to kick it. It can still be held normally as a two-handed object. Will bounce off any entity it collides with, including entities most wouldn't expect, like Hygroderes, Circuit Bees and Roaming Locusts.

spray paint.d: Spray paint is a tool item that can be used to paint walls and floors, as well as other surfaces such as on-ship furniture items and even other employees. A can of spray paint must be shaken before it can be used- otherwise, the paint will dissipate into the air instead of being applied.

sticky note.d: The Sticky note is a pedagogical item which generates in the ship, hidden just to the left of the Terminal. Its sole purpose is to reveal the otherwise hidden command SIGURD, which is used to read unlocked Sigurd Logs.

stop sign.d: The Stop Sign is a scrap item that can be used to hit and damage certain entities, similarly to the Shovel and Yield sign. It is heavier than the Shovel but otherwise functionally identical.

stun grenade.d: Stun grenades are explosive weapons intended to disorient entities. Upon being thrown, stun grenades will take 2.25 seconds to detonate, with anything caught in the blast being stunned for 7.5 seconds at base. tzp-inhalant.d: The TZP-Inhalant is a type of scrap that can be purchased from the store for credits. It temporarily increases an employee's speed, lowers the burden of their inventory weight, and reduces stamina drain when used by holding down left click. It can be used for 38 seconds before running out.

teeth.d: Teeth are a scrap item that continuously makes chattering noises when picked up. There is an 18% chance of disabling the noise when picked up. If dropped while chattering, it has a chance to move in a circular motion.

toothpaste.d: The Toothpaste item is an exclusive commodity found on the 5 most challenging moons within the game. Distinguished by its weightlessness, the Toothpaste item registers at on the scale. An interesting feature of this item is its atypical pricing range, fluctuating between and , a somewhat unusually broad spectrum in comparison to other items available.

toy robot.d: Robot toys are a scrap item that continuously makes loud toy noises when picked up. It can be picked up for a 25% chance of disabling the noise.

walkie-talkie.d: The Walkie-Talkie is used to communicate with co-workers beyond the proximity chat radius. It can transmit both voice and text (using the in-game chat) when activated.

whoopie cushion.d: Upon being walked over, the Whoopie Cushion emits a distinctive fart sound. It's essential to note that players are unable to activate the fart sound voluntarily when the item is held, it must be dropped and walked over. While the Whoopie Cushion may not yield significant value in terms of scrap, its appeal lies in its comedic value.

yield sign.d: A scrap item capable of hitting and damaging entities. Functions identically to the Stop Sign and Shovel items, but is significantly heavier than either of them, making it a less practical weapon.

zap gun.d: The Zap Gun is a type of scrap that can be purchased from the store for credits. It is a tool for stunning entities instead of directly damaging them.

zed dog.d: The Zed Dog is a plush fox that resembles ZedFox, the composer of the tracks "Boombox Song 5" and "Disco Ball" in Lethal Company.

mrov sauce.d: MorvDonalds' main scrap: about 101 credits each at 7 lb. The reason that moon is great money.

blank floppy disc.d: Craft on Galetry (2 Plastic stock, 1 Circuit boards, 3 Copper wiring). Insert into a moon's Floppy disc machine to make that moon's unlock disc (Selector, Dormant, Xenphir, Dune, Spine, Heap).

failsafe floppy disc.d: Under the right-hand counter of the Galetry gift shop (mod v7.0.0+). Translate it to re-unlock moons that vanished from your save.

vents.d: A fish-like creature that lives in water inside the facility (added in v80).
vents.s: Lives in water. Stay out of deep water where you can and kill it with a weapon or shovel (4 HP) if it comes for you.

vents.d: The Barber is a hostile indoor entity. It moves by intermittently hopping short distances, accompanied by a drumroll noise when preparing to move, and a honking sound upon moving.
vents.s: Use the Barber's snare and music to indicate when it'll attack. The note played when it moves is very loud, so listen to it to know where it is. In versions below 62: If you hear a barber, be prepared for another one to be close behind. They spawn in packs of two and stick close to each other due to the master barber system.

vents.d: The Bracken, colloquially known as the "Flowerman", is a hostile indoor entity. Quietly stalking an employee from behind at a distance, it will eventually approach and attempt to snap an employee's neck before dragging away their corpse. The moon they are most commonly found on is Vow.
vents.s: Diligently checking surroundings indoors will ensure the Bracken is unable to sneak up on employees. Once spotted, as long as employees neither approach nor stare, it will immediately flee further into the building. While it is evading, a faint descending hum sound will be heard as long as it can still see you; when this sound cuts out, it is safe to turn around.

vents.d: The Bunker Spider is a hostile indoor entity. After building a nest, it lies in wait to ambush employees who step into their webs. It then gives chase to employees approaching them or their traps, dealing immense damage and ensnaring them in a silk-covered cocoon if they are killed.
vents.s: Before Bunker Spiders lay their webs, they are best left alone, since they will not be aggressive unless provoked by going close. They will not lay webs when in close proximity to other employees. This also means it is possible for an employee to prevent the Bunker Spider from ever laying any webs, albeit doing so poses danger to said employee.

vents.d: The Butler is a hostile indoor entity. Initially appearing docile around groups of two or more employees while sweeping with a broom, it draws a knife to murder any employees that are left alone in a room with it. The moon they are most commonly found on is Dine.
vents.s: The Butler will not attack if another employee is nearby while keeping distance. Because of this, it is advised to stick together with at least one other employee if a Butler is present. If caught alone, it's ideal to run instead of fight as Butlers have a low attack cool down so they can get multiple hits in a short amount of time.

vents.d: The Cadaver Bloom is a hostile entity. It does not appear naturally, and instead grows out of an employee infected by the spores of Cadaver Growths.
vents.s: What an infected employee becomes. Spray Weed killer on infected teammates before 100% infection to cure them. If a Bloom appears, keep distance and fight it as a group; shotguns only do 1 damage to it.

vents.d: The Cadaver Growth is a tall, infectious fern entity that grows indoors. They spread autonomously at a quick rate and emit a cloud of spores wherever they are present.
vents.s: Plants that infect you. Spray them with Weed killer to destroy them and avoid walking through patches. Cure infected teammates with Weed killer before they reach 100%.

vents.d: The Coil-Head is a hostile indoor entity. It remains stationary when it is within an employee's line of sight, but chases and attacks nearby employees extremely quickly while not being observed. The moon they are most commonly found on is Offense.
vents.s: A group can have a single employee watch Coil-heads while others loot. This employee would have to be especially cautious of other enemies, as the employee would be severely inhibited by the Coil-heads' presence. Considering that an attacking Coil-head will always head for the nearest employee, it would be imperative to warn other employees of its presence.

vents.d: The Ghost Girl is a hostile indoor entity. Depending on a number of unique factors, it targets and haunts a specific employee for an extended period of time, before eventually chasing after the targeted employee and instantly killing them upon contact by decapitation.
vents.s: The Ghost Girl is one of the most consistently difficult threats a team can face. She is unique in that, once spawned in, there is no way to avoid interacting with her; she will always pick one employee to haunt at all times. Once an employee recognizes they are being haunted, they should alert their teammates as quickly as possible.

vents.d: The Hoarding Bug, colloquially known as the "Lootbug", is a hostile indoor entity. Often seen roaming the facility in large colonies, it collects and carries scrap to a specific location it considers as a nest.
vents.s: In most cases, Hoarding Bugs should be killed as soon as possible, to avoid scrap being taken far away or having to face several at once later. One bug can be killed relatively easily by hitting it once, then strafing to avoid its attack and hitting it two more times as it flies by; they are quite slow to turn. One or multiple can be taken out at once with one shotgun shot, if available.

vents.d: The Hygrodere is a hostile indoor entity. It moves slowly along the ground towards nearby employees or sources of noise while covering a large surface area, rapidly damaging employees upon contact. The moon they are most commonly found on is Offense.
vents.s: Because of the Hygrodere's slow speed, avoiding it is simple unless the employee becomes cornered or is dealing with other entities in the facility. The best course of action is to locate the Hygrodere and track its bubbling sounds to prevent being cornered. Once a Hygrodere has spotted an employee, it will always know their location, so employees should keep its continual pursuit in mind.

vents.d: The Jester is a hostile indoor entity. Initially, it passively searches for and follows a nearby employee before it randomly stops in place and starts cranking.
vents.s: Employees should establish an escape route out of the building when a Jester is discovered, and follow this route as soon as it enters its cranking state. Employees can safely re-enter the building once 5 seconds have passed after the last living employee is removed from the building, as the Jester will have reverted to its roaming state.

vents.d: The Maneater is a deceptively cute indoor entity resembling an insect. While it initially appears to be a sensitive, carriable infant requiring constant care and maintenance, it transforms into a monstrous, extremely fast and deadly enemy if upset or provoked.
vents.s: Since it can be carried in baby form, the Maneater can be neutralized by simply dropping it into certain pits, trapping it for the rest of the day. Deep pits within the cave system usually work, as well as the pit in the large elbow room in the Factory, but the mature form can teleport out of most other pits when transformed. As of v62, most of these "cheese" strategies have been blocked.

vents.d: Mask Hornets are entities found indoors that are spawned from killed Butlers. Once spawned, they roam the facility looking for employees and act similarly to Circuit bees. They stay in the facility until the ship leaves the moon.
vents.s: Guard a hive. Leave the hive alone unless you want it as scrap; if you grab it, run straight for the ship without stopping.

vents.d: The Masked, also referred to as the Mimic, is a hostile indoor entity. While capable of spawning naturally, it also spawns if an employee wears a mask for a certain period of time, causing them to become possessed.
vents.s: It is recommended if you see a Masked to create as much distance and open space as possible, along with making sure all employees know of its existence to not cause more Masked to spawn. Masked do not retain any Spray paint on them, allowing possible indication of possession. If an employee is transforming into a Masked, the animation of the possession is long enough for another employee to kill the Masked.

vents.d: The Nutcracker is a hostile indoor entity. It initially patrols and surveys its surroundings for any signs of movement. Upon detecting movement from a nearby entity or employee, it chases after them and uses a variety of deadly attacks, such as kicking or blasting the target with a shotgun.
vents.s: The Nutcracker can be a very dangerous adversary due to its extremely lethal shotgun that can instantly kill any employee caught out in the open, making cover a must for most fights with a Nutcracker. However, despite this danger the Nutcracker is usually an enemy worth killing, as the shotgun it drops is a very powerful weapon and can be sold to help meet quota.

vents.d: The Snare Flea is a hostile indoor entity. It attaches itself to the ceiling and waits for employees to approach it, before dropping to the floor and attempting to suffocate them by wrapping itself around their head. The moon they are most commonly found on is Assurance.
vents.s: Snare Fleas are either lethal or a mere annoyance depending on your current situation. Hitting one while it has grabbed a worker will knock it off, but they can be difficult to hit otherwise. With this in mind, you can hit it off a coworker, try to get another hit in, then drop your shovel for your fellow coworker you rescued to repeat the process if the Snare Flea grabs you.

vents.d: The Spore Lizard is a docile indoor entity. It flees from employees when spotted, and releases a dense cloud of spores from its tail or bites in self-defense when cornered. The moon they are most commonly found on is Experimentation.
vents.s: While the Spore Lizard may come across as intimidating, it most certainly isn't dangerous. It will only attack with a non-lethal bite in very close range, so an employee's best option is to simply respect it and leave it alone. The Spore Lizard will often hiss long before a employee even comes close enough for it to bite, so evading them is usually trivial.

vents.d: The Thumper, also known as the "Half" or internally as the "Crawler", is a hostile indoor entity. It is incapable of hearing and relies on eyesight to hunt down and attack employees, rapidly accelerating when moving and decelerating when turning corners or upon hitting a wall.
vents.s: Thumpers are quick and dangerous. They take 4 Shovel hits to kill and kills an employee in 4 quick bites. They are very fast, steadily gaining speed as they move forward, and lose some speed when turning. If handled poorly, they will reach speeds faster than can be outrun by any means. Taking sharp turns around many corners will significantly aid escape attempts.

vents.d: The Baboon Hawk is a hostile outdoor entity. It exhibits fiercely territorial behavior and becomes more aggressive if it has the company of others, or when employees are intruding on it or its territory.
vents.s: Try to make trips to/from The Ship in groups, whenever possible. Baboon Hawks will usually stay a decent way away from you before attacking, so boarding the ship and closing the doors will get them to back off or buy you some time at least. Making noise will attract Baboon Hawks in your direction if they are not more interested in something else.

vents.d: The Earth Leviathan, also known as the "Sandworm", is a hostile outdoor entity. Burrowing deep within the ground, it tracks the movements of nearby employees before suddenly erupting from the ground, instantly consuming anything in its path. The moon they are most commonly found on is Assurance.
vents.s: The presence of an Earth Leviathan can be ascertained by listening for underground groaning sounds, and its attack is telegraphed by a distinct low growl as particles of dirt jump out of the ground. An Earth Leviathan cannot be killed and is present on every moon, so caution should be taken during nighttime when roaming outside.

vents.d: The Eyeless Dog is a hostile outdoor entity. Commonly found roaming in packs, it is completely blind, and instead uses its exceptional hearing to hunt down and ruthlessly maul employees who alert it to their presence. The moon they are most commonly found on is Titan.
vents.s: Spotting Eyeless dogs from afar, players can maneuver around them without alerting them through noise. Alternatively, crouch walking (which eliminates sound made through moving), remaining silent and out of Eyeless dogs' path to avoid a head-on collision allows players to pass by without detection.

vents.d: The Feiopar, internally known as the "Puma", is a hostile outdoor entity. Often seen hunting in packs, it slowly stalks and approaches its prey from behind, before tearing them to pieces with its claws once it gets close.
vents.s: Fast outdoor predator at night. Get back to the ship before dark, move in groups and carry a weapon (4 HP).

vents.d: The Forest Keeper, also known as the "Forest Giant" or simply "Giant", is a hostile outdoor entity. While unable to hear sounds, it relies on an enhanced line of sight to detect and pursue employees, before capturing them in its grasp and eating them whole.
vents.s: Staying crouched and avoiding their line of sight using the environment (such as hiding behind trees and rocks) will avoid employees alerting a Forest Keeper of their presence. If you are in a Keeper's line of sight, you will hear a continuous low-pitched horror ambience, as if you just saw a Bracken; use this as your cue to break line of sight.

vents.d: The Kidnapper Fox, known internally as the "Bush Wolf", is a hostile outdoor entity. It hides within patches of Vain Shrouds, residing within the largest patch and ambushing approaching employees.
vents.s: If a Kidnapper Fox encounters a group of employees, it may attempt to latch its tongue onto one of them and drag the employee away to devour soon after. Because of this, it's important to always have one member of the group carry a shovel to help any employees that get grabbed.

vents.d: The Old Bird, also known as Al (A16-L31) or the "Walking Ransom Letter", is a hostile outdoor entity. While initially appearing inert, it reactivates after either a certain period of time passes or when the apparatus is unplugged from the facility.
vents.s: Old Birds can usually be a benefit, killing off dangerous creatures for you. Doing your best to avoid it entirely while this happens is vital to making it an advantage instead of a detriment. If spotted, running in a small semi-circle around it to force it to slowly turn while you gain ground is a good way to lose it. Getting behind cover before it turns to face you can make it lose you entirely.

vents.d: Circuit Bees, also known as Red Bees, are hostile outdoor entities. In order to protect their hive, they attack employees that approach them or their hive by conducting electricity, and become enraged if the hive is stolen or they are otherwise unable to return to it.
vents.s: Circuit Bees will not be a major problem for employees not intending to collect their hives, and being vigilant about walking into the radius of a beehive is the most strategy that will be necessary to avoid death. However, taking a Circuit Bees' hive is almost always worth it if you have time, as it is usually very high value. For more details on hive collection, consult the Bee Hive Strategy section.

vents.d: The Giant Sapsucker, also known internally as the "Giant Kiwi", is a hostile outdoor entity. It is a potentially dangerous threat that protects its nest containing three eggs, rapidly attacks employees who get too close to its nest, and becomes enraged if its eggs are taken from it.
vents.s: Taking Sapsucker eggs, although highly valuable, is an extremely risky move and usually not worth it if you intend on keeping the Giant Sapsucker alive, because it essentially forces you to leave the moon after you have stolen an egg, due to its ability to break into the ship. If you would still like to try to take its eggs, there are many different methods to acquiring them.

vents.d: Manticoils are passive ambient birds found outdoors. With a distinctive four-winged anatomy, they can be seen soaring overhead or hopping on the ground either alone or in small groups.
vents.s: Harmless bird. Ignore it, or kill it with one shovel hit for its body as scrap.

vents.d: Roaming locusts are small harmless insects found outdoors swarming in spherical formations.
vents.s: Harmless swarm that scatters when you get close. Just walk through.

vents.d: The Tulip Snake is an outdoor daytime entity. It lunges at and clings to employees before carrying them into the air and eventually dropping them, and comes in multiple colors. The moon they are most commonly found on is Adamance.
vents.s: Unlike most entities, Tulip Snakes can be extremely helpful for an employee who knows how to use them to their advantage. By purposely chasing and getting Tulip Snakes to attach, and then timing a jump as they begin to flap allows employees to quickly traverse cliffs, long stretches of terrain, or get to places normally inaccessible.

lore.title: Acidir
lore.intro:
Acidir used to be home to the rich collectors of mysterious artifacts. It is reported that these collectors have recently stumbled upon something truly mysterious. We don't know exactly what it is, all we know is that no sane voice was heard after its arrival. High value artefacts remain inside.
There are 12 new themed scrap items to find on this moon.

secs.html: - A crescent shaped cosmic growth with eyes all over it.
- These follow the descent into madness of Acidir's inhabitants after the Crescent of Curses shows up.

Image & Text ⁠
It has been a strange past few days.
Of course that is the usual around here but some things appear off.
Stranger than usual.

We noticed that the water filters have been burnt through.
There was a substantial buildup in acidir material in the pipelines.
Luckilly no leakages but it is strange how none of us noticed the.. acidic taste in the water supply.
We have been drinking this for days.

Image & Text ⁠
Things are getting weirder.
It has only been slightly over a week since the renowned Crescent of Curses arrived on our doorstep.

I fear unlike the other artefacts we collected, this one appears to radiate some sort of aura which messes with the brain.

At least the filter has been replaced.
Unfortunately it was only after one of us took a warm bath and melted overnight.

We need to get rid of that thing.

Image & Text ⁠
We should never have accepted that Crescent of Curses.
Some of us have gone mad!

This morning we discovered three more skeletons at the bottom of the lakes.
I fear out of sheer madness they went for an acidic swim.

I too have experienced some strange things.
Sometimes when I look down a hallway, it starts expanding.
Like there are more than a million other ways to go.

It shows things that nobody can see.

SO MANY HALLWAYS

CURSES CURSES CURSES CURSES CURSES
CURSES CURSES CURSES CURSES CURSES
CURSES CURSES CURSES CURSES CURSES
CURSES CURSES CURSES CURSES CURSES

HAHAHAHAHAHAHA

IT IS WATCHING ME

NOWHERE TO GO

IT IS COMING

THE BIG EYE IN THE SKY

IT SEES US ALL

- Captain Commander Cunningham's report on Acidir during her second expedition in hopes of finding Cosmocos, can be found by following the spotlights next to a fire exit.

Text ⁠
Captains Log. Log 3. Location, Acidir.

I’ve hardly had a moment to record my findings.
Navigating Etern was a nightmare with those bloody Nutcrackers roaming the desert.
We were down to a crew of 26 after that veritable screw-up - and I’m afraid things have only gotten worse since we arrived on Acidir.
But first - my findings on Etern.

A silver lining - I recovered a log from the corpse of a scientist pertaining to Cosmocos’ location.
It seems that he created some sort of AI for the sole purpose of retrieving these coordinates.
Unfortunately, the AI seems to malfunction while reciting them...

Certainly, it’s some system error in the mad-man’s machine.
Most definitely.
But...for some reason, it feels to me that Cosmocos...does not want to be found.
And yet the more I recall, the more intense my desire becomes to try and locate it.
To see the way the walls of crystal shimmer in the light of those strange bulbs that hang from the trees...

I know that my dreary mind couldn’t create things of such beauty of its own accord.
I’m far too boring for that.

Nevertheless.
I left a log with the rising map on Atlantica, and I’ve discovered that the 6th letter of the coordinates is a lowercase Z. Zee. Zed.

We’ll soon be leaving Acidir.
5 went mad after coming into contact with the Crescent of Curses and decided to go for a swim with the local pond life.
3 ran screaming into the woods, and it’s been hours since we saw them.
The ship will fly soon when the conditions become too dangerous.
If they’re not back before then...

Our next destination is Polarus.
This was the closest moon to Cosmocos before it’s disappearance.
We’ll stop by Gratar in lieu of the ramblings in the scientists log.

This is Cunningham. Signing off.

This videotape can be found on Alcatras, Junic and Gloom.

Text ⁠
Tape 4, Acidir.
This is Captain Cunningham.

When we arrived here the crew seemed fine.
I use the term fine very loosely here.. They managed.

However I feel the longer we stay, the worse things seem to be getting.
I'm not sure if it's the air, the manor or the lakes of acid. But a few of us have already gone missing.

I rate Acidir an S.
Cunningham, signing off.

lore.title: Alcatras
lore.intro: Alcatras has a prison island in the outter area of the known region. Only the most dangerous of criminals would be sent to this place to never be heard from again. It is well protected, the Mortor brand was quite popular.

secs.html: Alcatras holds lore items such as:
found on Alcatras paint the story of a man wrongfully convicted for the murder of his family and his experiences inside the prison.

Image & Text ⁠
I found some pen and paper stached below my cold, hard mattress.
Meaning I can FINALLY write down some of my problems with this BROKEN justice system.

For one, I AM INNOCENT!
I would never EVER do that to my wife and children.
And the fact that they never even had a look at the evidence I provided.
HORRID!

If I ever get the opportunity to het out of this hell hole..
I will sue the everliving hell out of those people.
Justice my ass.

Meanwhile I'm sure that monster is still out there.
AGHH
What he did to my children, my Jane..

If I ever find him I'll be happy to watch him ROT behind these same bars that I find myself behind.
HE belongs in a cell on Alcatras NOT ME!

Though unfortunately they gave me life in prison.
I don't think I'll ever be able to get true justice.

Image & Text ⁠
I remember that moment... clear as day.
I was at work when I received a message from my wife Jane.'There's people in the house'.
I told her to grab the gun from my desk and hide with the kids in the bedroom closet.
'I am on my way' I said.

While driving home I got a call from my nextdoor neighbor.
She said she heard screams and gunshots from our apartment.
And that her husband called the police.
I should have never gone home after I heard that...

When I finally got home, I burst through the door and...
I found her..
On the floor in the kitchen..
She had been shot multiple times and her body was partially flayed.

And before I could even see what he did to my children, the cops ran in and I was arrested on the spot.

But as we drove away. I saw him I SAW HIM.
His crooked smile and those fiery eyes staring at me through the bushes, still covered in Jane's blood.

I will never forget that face.

Image & Text ⁠
I've been here for six weeks now.
They told me there will be a retrial for my case!
THANK GOD!
Maybe this time they will actually have a close look at all the evidence I've provided.
This also means I can FINALLY leave this place.
Even if temporarily.

We're also slowly being moved to another prison I've heard.
I really hope it's a little nicer because I am SICK of waking up to a swarm of rats running around our cells.

The activities here are horrible too.
We can't even work out since most of the equipment is either broken or extremely dirty.

They cleared out a couple cell blocks already.
I think we might be next.

This does mean I'll have to leave my notes here.
I don't think I can sneak those with me.

I will find justice for you Jane.
I loved you.

Alongside the Prisoner Notes, a Guard's Note can be found which explains the fate of all prisoners on Alcatras.

Image & Text ⁠
This poor guy didn't deserve this.
I wonder if there are any other innocent prisoners here.

If I knew this I would've made sure he wasn't put with the others.
But.
We're all just following orders here.

It's vile what we do here.
Poor guy thought he'd be moved.
We don't keep prisoners here.
We kill them and turn their bodies into soil.
Soil which is used to grow crops at an extraordinary rate.
These crops are then sold back to the public.

People would go crazy if they knew about this.
I would too.
But that's just our job.

I hate it but.. it's how money gets made.

lore.title: Asteroid-13
lore.intro: Asteroid-13 is not a traditional moon, but an asteroid housing a "bio-weapon testing facility". The moon orbits Vow and nobody who has ever went to the moon has returned.

secs.html:
Asteroid-13 is a bio-weapon testing and holding facility created after the fall of Calist. It hosted multiple entities such as:

BIO-HXNV7 (The description matches that of a Coil-head)

Cursed Coin (Effects of this bio-weapon match that of the Ghost Girl)

Hyper Acid (It is hinted towards the Acid having a connection with the Hydrodere through it's capabilities)

Comedy Mask (The Masks found throughout the vanilla game)

Golden Dagger (Custom item added by Welsey's Moons)

On the outside and throughout it's interior multiple pieces of information such as the following can be found:

Experiment Logs

Recovered Secret Log

Geoffrey Final Log

Prior to the Obscurity update, this log could spawn as random scrap within the interior of Asteroid-13. Logging it into the Log Translator unlocked Cosmocos. It is unknown if this log can still be acquired legitimately.

Scientist: Year 154, uh day 73.
I've found cosmocos.
Uh..

Found by following the red flares on the surface of Asteroid-13. Logging this tape continues Geoffrey's reversed storyline, unlocking Junic.

Text ⁠
I am Geoffrey Samuel Smith, Agent and high commander working directly for the Emperor.
This will be my final message.

Until recent I have believed that my actions since the Catalyst under command of the Emperor were for some greater good.
I was led to believe that all the sacrifices made were with purpose.
Yet they were in vain.
It wasn’t until I had lost all that I had left in my world when I realized.

I now find myself here to execute one final mission.
One of my own.
Over the past few months we have been collecting the many experimental bioweapons that were created because of me.
I made them believe we got them to study them further. Make them more dangerous.
That’s what the emperor would have wanted.
But I will no longer follow the wishes of that man.
He sits on his golden throne while everyone else suffers by his command.
I should have done something when he told me to give the order.
I should have executed him right then and there.

Back in the labs I smashed the glass containers for BIO-HXNV7, the deadliest weapon we have.
It will hopefully kill or convert most of the people here.
These loyal rats who think they’re on the winning side.
There is no winning side.
And I’ll make sure nobody will escape this place.
Nobody will use these atrocities to further this pointless hell!

I called for a facility wide decontamination.
And all of it will burn!

This videotape will always spawn on Galetry.

Text ⁠
The contents of this protectious highly classified material and expects for your eyes only.

There's a bioweapon testing facility on an asteroid orbiting 56-Vow.

The facility contains artifacts and experimental bioweapons ready for deployment.

You are tasked with investigating, containing and collecting these experiments.

If a member is lost do not try to attempt rescue, the mission is your FIRST and ONLY priority.

The status of this weapons is unclear.

Beware of anything that moves, walks, talks, bleeds, tears, CRIES, SCREAMS, SEEMS OUT OF PLACE, IF YOU WISH TO RETURN WITH YOUR WHOLE BODY STILL INTACT.

The Unified Dominion wishes you: GOOD LUCK

lore.title: Atlantica
lore.intro: Atlantica was hit by rogue rays from a supernova. This caused a disturbance in the local flow of time. Because of this, the city of Atlantica is forever doomed to sink over and over. Every inhabitant has drowned.

secs.html: Atlantica holds pieces of lore such as:
Wet Notes - these explain the neverending cycle that this moon is doomed to, written by one of it's inhabitants before succumbing to the same fate as all the others.

Image & Text ⁠
I woke up to screams of terror.
The city is sinking!

All is flooded we need to leave.\nOnly the bridge can save us!

... The bridge is gone. No hope.
I need to find a higher point.
Goodbye

Image & Text ⁠
I woke up to screams of terror.
The city is sinking!

All is flooded we need to leave.
Will the bridge be gone?

It's gone! I need to find a higher point.
Goodbye

Image & Text ⁠
I woke up to screams of terror. But less than in my dreams.
The city is sinking! Again!

Something is wrong.. This is.. unnatrual.
All who died are gone this time.
I saw a platform rise around 5pm.
I need to find a higher point.
That way I will survive.

Image & Text ⁠
It's all real! Every time!.
The city sinks but at midnight, the city returns.
But all who die stay dead.

I am the only one left!
The hallway is flooding again.

I might not make it this time.

Around 05:45 PM a platform can be seen rising from the water. This platform holds Cunningham's Travel Log 2 as well as a map of Cosmocos.

- Captain Commander Cunningham's report on Atlantica during her second expedition in hopes of finding Cosmocos.

Text ⁠
Captain’s Log. Log 2. Location, Atlantica.

After visiting Etern, we diverted course to Atlantica due to reports of ‘unnatural occurrences’ having taken place here.
And I’m glad we did - most excitingly, we have discovered a map of Cosmocos on this small island not far from the mainland.
We lost a crewmate trying to swim over and resorted to using jetpacks instead.
And despite our loss... seeing some evidence of Cosmocos was exhilarating.
It solidifies in my mind that these weren’t just delusions of mine, it was real.
I was there.
I saw it.
I’m familiar with this terrain.
I may not be able to recall with perfect clarity, but it is knowledge I possess.
Or... possessed.

Also of significant note - a body was discovered on Etern along with a log not dissimilar to mine.
I believe we’ve obtained another piece of the puzzle, so to speak.
I’ve etched it into the map.
Please excuse my haste, Atlantica is sinking and I must return to the ship.

Our course is set for Acidir.
With one less crewmate, we should be vigilant.

Cunningham, signing off.

There are two pushable bridges on exterior. One is just a shortcut to the ship but the other one will reveal a hidden tower that where you can find map of Lecaro on the ground. After interacting with it a strange audio will play. After that Lecaro will be unlocked for you.

Image & Text ⁠
Between the crystalline caverns, crossing the river of flame, is the right way, through the mines of Lecaro.

This videotape can be found on Alcatras, Thalasso and Gratar.

Text ⁠
Tape 2, Atlantica.

This is Captain Cunningham.
Going to Atlantica wasn't something we had initially planned. It was purely our curiosity that has led us here.

As of now we have not yet encountered anything unnatural as the reports have said.
However, I do feel something is off about this place. It is pretty but something in me is telling me to leave.

So far I would rate this place a C.
However I might've changed my mind by the time we go.
Cunningham, signing off.

lore.title: Berunah
lore.intro:
Endless deserts, nothing but sand.

Except for the occasional temple hidden between the hills of sand.

They say below the sand lies an ancient civilisation hidden from time.

secs.html:
Text ⁠
He. Is. Watching.
He has his eye.. directly.. upon you.
You disturbed his temple.. and he is angry.

I have been trying to rid this universe of this being for longer than you can imagine.

The things you see..
They aren't real, ignore them.
He is trying to melt your mind.

I can help you, if you help me.

Bring these seeds to their designated celestial bodies.
It will distract him for long enough.

Once that's done.. return..
And I will make my move.

Sometimes a sacrifice is needed.. to banish evil.. for good.

Image & Text ⁠
The stones of purification

These stones hold incredible power.
Through the crystal growing within, it can be used to alter matter.

To rid food of mold, crops of insects, water of plagues.
It can speed the growth of plants, heal the wounded, increase their strength.

Only when put together in precise ways can their power be used.

Image & Text ⁠
The purifying shrine

This device was designed to harvest and project the power of the purifying stones and spread their effect across areas far and wide.

The farmers most often used these to stabilize their farmland and increase the rate at which their crops grew.

lore.title: Calist
lore.intro: The Grand Capitol of Calist rests between the dense green forests and the lakes of golden shine. Until one day, it did not. Broken remains.. remain inside.

secs.html:
Calist, once a thriving population, left only as an empty shell of what it once was by the triton military's attacks.

There are multiple moon specific items found on Calist such as:

- Geoffrey Samuel Smith - agent working directly under The Emperor and his log on the use of bio-weapons being brought up to the council:

Text ⁠
We are now four weeks into the debate meaning next week will be the final and deciding council conference.
While the Council of Rule is still highly against the study and use of biological warfare, there must be a way to convince them otherwise.
..I understand that it is a very dangerous idea which..
In theory..
Could ruin more lives than I can count as well as cause a financial catastrophe within this region..

But I trust the Emperor knows this and I am sure he has a plan which I will be made aware of soon.
He does not sit upon the throne without reason.

After this log I might write a letter to my wife Madeline as I will be leaving 235-Calist the next morning for a meeting with the Emperor.
I hope to find some clarity about his plans to better structure our case.

Agent G- Signing off.

- Michael's Resignation Letter from the Council:

Image & Text ⁠
To start off my statement I would like everyone to remember why the use of biological warfare was made illegal in the first place.
Not two hundred years ago, over in the Altra region when the study and use of biological weapons was allowed still.
A conflict between two dominions turned to bloodshed. This war is now known as one of the most devastating wars in all of time across the known regions.

And it was the weaponry they used which marked this war as the deadliest one in history thus far.
The most commonly used was the melting gas made with the spores of an acidic super-fungi.
When it touched the skin or was inhaled, it would melt the victim from the inside out. And the majority of victims were not military but civilians.

Surely I do not speak for myself when I say-
This musn't happen again.
- Michael Dunton - an acting chairman of the council, and his experiences on Calist before the war:

Image & Text ⁠
I understand that I am writing on an official document but I have overheard something I feel like I shouldn't have. However it seems important enough to have it written down for later.
While I walked through the halls near the office secions. I heard a faint discussion through one of the closed doors.
It was the Emperor talking to his closest agent.

While I do not exactly recall what was said, I do remember them discussing the case as it stands. Their strategy is unusual.
The agent seemed sceptical while the Emperor remained adamant. Understandibly so.

Apparently their next argument will be that biological weapons might come in use if, say, a swarm of unidentified lifeforms from beyond the known regions invade that of ours.
Not impossible but certainly not plausible.

I am going to try figuring out more about the Emperor's plans.

Image & Text ⁠
I followed him through the vast halls of this citadel, hoping to see if he revealed anything else.
But when I turned the corner, he had vanished into one of the storage rooms. Which is particularly strange I thought.
And when I put my ear up against the door. I heard him talk again.

He sounded rather monotone. Having a discussion with himself.
Or so I thought.
It wasn't until he said 'my overseer' when I realised he was talking to someone or.. something.

I hid around the corner when he left the storage closet. And he quietly mumbled 'The seed must grow' as he left the hallway.
I am uncertain what any of this means but I feel something larger is a play here.

Image & Text ⁠
I, Michael Dunton hereby resign from my position on the council.

I feel there are things at play that are bigger than they seem.
While I am certain that I would not be believed if I brought this up myself, I have left my notes and recordings in my office.

I do not wish to be part of what's happening or what's to come.
Strange things are going on in this council, and in this case.

During the 4th and previous conference it seems to me that all sense of logistics are thrown out the window.
I will take my leave on the day of the 5th and final conference.

It is best to carry my words with heavy thought.

-Michael Dunton

Then project Mycete will be perfect. The soldiers we produce will be impenetrable, unstoppable. We will rescue so many cities from their lawlessness. We will unite what’s left after the silent age. You can stop the engineer, but not his machine.
C. Darter: You’re lost, Sol. You’re lost in your own fantasy.
S. Underhill: Don’t you see it? The cities we’ve saved? The people exist in peace. We brought them that peace. We’ve perfected it. You give people too much will, they destroy themselves. You give them too little, they destroy their government. You give them just enough, they’re happy. It doesn’t even have to be real. History is an archive of mistakes, an encyclopedia of lessons, we are the only ones who chose not to ignore them.
C. Darter: You can’t call it peace when you’re the one bringing war. Maybe I can’t stop the project. But I can stop you.
—----------------------- 
Emergency recording ended

This recording can randomly spawn as scrap within the interior.

Text ⁠
It strikes a fear in me, rooted deep within my ocean of thought. He kept asking about it and I don't even have the full answer. They have a way of operating that makes them invisible to not only the surface but even those who'd consider themselves high up the ladder. But I know they're here. They're everywhere. Stare long enough into the abyss, you start seeing things. Holes in reality. Fissures in logic. Yet you shake your head and pretend it was your eyes playing tricks on you. I see them. Companies appear more and more frequent like an infestation of roaches from influential businessmen to lower class entrepreneurs. All with history, documents, lives. Processed within our systems. It's usual. Standard practice. Nothing strange about it. But you look closer. You read their documents. Everything seems normal until.. you get a glimpse. A date mismatched. A name changed. Manlike mistakes, for sure. Look deeper, closer. Children without proof of birth. Deposits from companies that only registered days later. Trades between people who don't even know each other. Fissures. I've never observed them, my superiors have never seen them. Only stories.. irregularities. Seemingly random. But I think they are connected. They're here. And I believe they're scared. There is something here that scares them, threatens them. Makes them slip up. And if something is here that scares the corporate entity that’s able to twist our reality no matter where in our galaxy. You best know I sleep with one eye open.

lore.title: Core

If players land on Core in the future on that save file, a mild outbreak of white mold will be present on the exterior and Infected Bunker Spiders will spawn on the exterior at the start of the day.

- continue the story of the prisoner Pedro from Dreck. Disguising as a guard, Pedro successfully was able to get revenge on and kill the man who imprisoned him, felt empty after doing so, and died to a gunshot wound shortly afterward. They can be found as scrap within the interior.

Image & Text ⁠
It worked. My disguise was enough to make them believe I was with them. I have been assigned a room in the guard chambers.
This facility is much larger.
The clouds seem to end before the building does.
The conditions are not better either. I feel for the workers.
In some places it's warm enough to melt skin off muscle.

Now I'm here I will need to get accustomed to the standard procedures. I will also need to study the building a bit more before I can start planning anything.
Not to mention figure out where Jareck is among all of this.

One way or another.

Despite what it might seem from the perspective of the workers below.
Being a guard here is a different kind of imprisoning.
Instead of constant physical labour you're put through committing actions that'll break a man.
While I don't share the same chains as those below.
I feel just as shackled.

However, I know my way to the upper layers.
I have seen him. He takes two smoke breaks by the left most fire exit at the bottom. Usually around 11 AM and 7 PM.
The only place that's not monitored here is a small storage closet near the stairs atop the upper floor.
If I can sneak in there. With the right timing...
I can give him what he deserves.

This is writ with bloodied hands.
Parts of Jareck's brain still between my fingernails.
I succeeded.

My chest is bleedin. A searing pain from one side to the other. I believe he shot me in my ambush.
Though I only geel it now.
My adrenaline kept me going. I was on top of him.
Every fist that struck his face was fueled by unmatched anger.
I asked what happened to my wife and child..
He didn't even know who I was.
I now realise the road I drove would lead to nowhere.
I killed the man I hated so much.
Yet nothing's changed. I feel no different.
My family is still missing. And soon my breath will be my last.
I was damned from the day I was taken.

As per usual, I leave a note.
I'm only getting closer to completing my task.
The cancer that grows within me makes me feel weaker by the day.
But I must continue.
He will heal me.

I must say I enjoyed the peace that Dreck brought me.
It was cold yet empty. It felt like nothing was there to bother me.
I felt alone but.. the good kind.
I really.. needed that.
The war had quite a toll on me. Even if it's all I know.
I mean. I was practically created by it.
Just like many others.

... I should get the fuel I came here for and proceed to Faith.

lore.title: Cosmocos
lore.intro: Cosmocos is the long lost moon. Home to one of the Vault Key Apparati and to the Celestial Brain.

secs.html: Forgotten logs 1-3 can be found as random scrap in the interior, while Forgotten log 4 is found next to the Celestial Brain.

Text ⁠
At the behest of Captain Donahue, I am to record my own personal experiences here on Cosmocos.

I was first to stumble upon this strange extraterrestrial lifeform.
It seemed to be, upon first glance, perhaps a plant, or something akin to coral - something like Diploria.
But when I placed my hand upon it, even through my suit, I felt - I felt as if incredible knowledge was poured into me.
Knowledge of things vastly unfamiliar and unbelievably alien to me - but also of things familiar, things around me that others had been educated on, but I’d never had the opportunity to learn.
It was incredible, exhilarating.
Unlike anything I’ve ever experienced.

But the most exhilarating thing of all was this unusual connection I feel that I’ve fostered with this thing.
This being.
In a sense, it felt... like a person, is perhaps the best way to put it, in terms we are capable of understanding.
Like Cosmocos isn’t just a moon.
Like it’s... a huge, alien life-form, sitting here in space with its own incredible ecosystem.

Bizarre as it may be, I can say with confidence that I could feel what seemed to be a rush of emotions from Cosmocos itself.
I still feel it now, in truth.
Which sounds like insanity, doesn’t it? But it was beautiful.
Like a rush of warmth, kindness, generosity.
I really feel like Cosmocos wants to teach us things.
Like it wants to help us grow and nurture us.

The Captain has commanded that no one is to interact with this celestial brain aside from himself for our own safety.
I do feel slightly disheartened by this, as I was hoping to commune with it again.

I have so much more to say.
It’ll be difficult to record all of this knowledge I’ve been gifted with in a comprehensible format on these recorders, but I’ll do my best over the next few cycles.

Lieutenant Commander Cunningham, signing off.

Text ⁠
There has been a terrible turn of events.

The whole crew is celebrating, currently, after the Captain has confirmed my mad ramblings to be based in truth.
That Cosmocos possesses incredible alien knowledge, and is willing to share it with us.
Granted - initially, I was not entirely coherent when I tried to convey my experience with the celestial brain, but...tch, I’ll hold my tongue.

He’s ordered to remove the brain and prepare for it to be taken back with us to 61-March.
But this will kill Cosmocos, I know this for certain.
Slowly, over time, atrophied, until it is a husk.
I don’t know why the Captain, having been offered the same kindness from Cosmocos, would even consider doing something like this.
It’s not right.
Perhaps he doesn’t know?
Perhaps we were not offered the same thing?
Perhaps he knows...and he doesn’t care?
He’s not a man known for his kindness, after all.

I asked that we put it to a vote.
Not a single person sided with me.

I don’t know what to do.
I don’t know what I could possibly do to dissuade the Captain that wouldn’t have me thrown in a pod set on course for a jail cell back on 61.

But I have to do something.
This isn’t what Cosmocos wants.
And I refuse to see it die like this.

Lieutenant Commander Cunningham, signing off.

Text ⁠
He threatened me! That- that- heartless-

I don’t know why I ever felt compelled to try and convince that man of anything, knowing he is capable of such evil.
He is not a man reasoned with.

Cosmocos has the most beautiful terrain I’ve ever laid eyes upon.
Such gorgeous, diverse plant life.
A heart.
I really feel as though it has what the more spritual of us would call a soul.
And the Captain has a gall to suggest that Cosmocos has tricked me, somehow.

Perhaps these feelings are not my own.
Perhaps these are feelings Cosmocos has imposed upon me.

Regardless of whether these emotions are pre-disposed or not - with everyone ounce of my being, I feel certain that Cosmocos is a thinking, feeling moon.
Isn’t that incredible?
Shouldn’t that be protected?

I’m going to be the one to protect it, if no one else will.

Whatever the cost.
If I fail, at worst, they’ll send me back to March for proper proceedings.
My knowledge is too valuable.

And then I’ll make it my mission to come back.
If they succeed in doing this to Cosmocos...
I’ll see it done that it is made whole again.

Cunningham, signing off.

Text ⁠
Long time no see, old friend.

You gave me a real run-around, didn’t you?
Going off the radar like that.
You teleported yourself... nearly eight-hundred-million miles away.
I didn’t even know you could do that.
You are full of wonders.

You didn’t want to hurt them, did you, friend?

You did everything you could not to kill them.
You wanted so dearly to see them learn, and grow, and help each other...

I feel it. I know, I know...

They’re still out there, though, aren’t they?
That’s them?
Lurking in the shadows.
They’re protecting you now.

I want to protect you too, if you’ll let me.
No one will ever hurt you again.

Not while I’m around.

Our team has gone mad. Ever since the flash, our technology seems to be malfunctioning.
It is unlikely that we’ll be able to leave anytime soon.
Day 80
A few on the team say they are experiencing disorientation and dizziness. Unsure as to why but it appears to be a common factor. I wonder if we’ve been hit with a large surge of radiation. We best figure out what’s wrong with the equipment so we can do a proper evaluation.

Three of us stumbled into the forest, they said, “the forest is calling to us”. If it weren’t for the fact that we need all hands on deck I would let them get lost. I’ve sent two more of us out to go and look for them.

Nobody turned up, not the three who went missing nor the ones I sent out to find them. Fantastic. Now I am starting to sense it too. Slightly disoriented and there’s this strange feel to my skin.
I’ve told the rest of the team to keep working on getting the equipment fixed up. I’m heading out to the third facility. It’s not too distant. About 12000 meters north-east from here.
Perhaps they have answers there.

My skin feels strange. My back hurts. It feels like something’s crawling under my shoulderblades. The path seems different from what we mapped out. I dare say I am lost.
Running out of ink too.

Everything hurts. My legs below my knees are shrinking. It’s getting hard to walk. My skin has turned purple and thick. There’s something sticking out my back. Something cursed me, something cursed all of us. I don’t believe I’ll be here for much longer. There’s something very wrong here.
I think I’ll just sit by this tree. I’ll write more tomorrow.

lore.title: Desolation
lore.intro: Not much is known about this asteroid, nobody has dared to visit it since its sudden appearance. Hence it has not been properly named, all we know is that it's a very dangerous place. A place completely desolate of life. For its name is: Desolation.

secs.html: Desolation was originally part of Cosmocos and housed a secondary facility there. When Cosmocos began its teleportation, it split off this segment to protect itself from any surviving personnel in the secondary facility.

Harrington's Logs can randomly spawn as scrap within the interior. They follow the story of Professor Harrington, a scientist who was researching Cosmocos and its "Cosmic Growth" in this secondary facility and experienced its teleportation.

Text ⁠
uh, we really need to get better voice recorders for this.
uhh anyways, yesterday we have finally concluded construction of the secondary research facillity here.
The equipment will arrive in a few days from now. Then we can offically start studdying on this side of the moon.
Which is splendid because have made a recent discovery...
This weird stuff..
Some sort of fungi perhaps?

I am not entirely sure what this is just yet but it has a.. regenerative ability.. at speeds unlike anything we have seen before.

We discovered this when we used a metal pipe to carefully stab a hole into it.
Anwyays.
I should wrap this up now, I'll record another log once we've got something.

Professor Harrington, over and out.

Text ⁠
Well, we found something.

It appears this strange growth is neither a fungi.. nor its own organism.
It's its own new thing.
It is able to remember certain growing patern from a genetic blueprint.
Meaning it's alive!
But seamingly not in the traditional way we precieve living things.
Our entire understanding of life was just flipped upside down.
It is even able to grow these weird.. bulbs resembling eyes.
It is unsure if these eyes serve a purpose.. Well.. They must.. Otherwise it wouldn't be growing them.

We will refer to this as.. Cosmic Growth from now on.
That's all I can say for now.

Professor Harrington, over and out.

Text ⁠
These old voice recorders are the worst..
Right..
We've got word from captain Donahue over at the primary facility.
They have found.. something..
It appears to be something new, something unexplored.
They think it might be some sort of plant which sounds exciting.

Here however we've made steady progress.
As mentioned before, this cosmic growth is able to grow.. eyes wherever it pleases.
At first we thought it might be some sort of defense mechanism.
But there's no active predators on Cosmocos from the data we've gathered.
But then we noticed something strange..

One of the eyes growing in our incubators was able to move and look around, illuminating whatever it looked at.
This place is full of surprises.
More information soon.

Professor Harrington, over and out.

It's been a strange past few weeks, we've heard that luitenant commander Cunningham was send back to 61 after going mad.

well..
not a definitive one at least.

It's certainly strange.
I wonder if the-

*Rumbling*

What is happening?
Everything is bright outside??

Woah.
What's happening.

There's a what coming at us?!

*The sounds of a moon ripping itself apart.*

We have been hit.
Worse.

I..
I need to go..

lore.title: Dreck
lore.intro: The salt fields of Dreck were most popular for prison mining camps. The working conditions were harsh, nowhere near as harsh as those on Core however. Though despite the enforcement of the military, one of the quarries was overtaken by its prisoners.

secs.html: After logging the Floppy disk, which can be acquired on various other moons, a journal entry for Dreck will be sent to the terminal that details a mission debrief for soldiers dispatched from Trite to stop the rebelling prisoners.

Pedro's notes tell the story of the prisoner Pedro, who came up with the escape plan, is responsible for the gas leaks, and is seeking revenge on the man who imprisoned him. At least one of each note is guaranteed to spawn within the interior.

lore.title: Empra
lore.intro: Home of the Emperor. Empra is happiness. Happiness is Empra.

secs.html:
Images & Text ⁠
Diary entry 847.

Nothing quite remarkable today.

10:30 I woke up and per usual I brushed my teeth, did my hair, changed my clothes and went out for breakfast with the family in the grand hall. Had a laugh with my dad and went back home.

11:40 The cleaners knocked apparently, they should know to use the light by now. How many times would it take for them to remember I can’t hear the knocking.

13:30 We are back out to get lunch. I’ve been practicing art in the meantime. My parents are keen on letting me know it’s a worthless skill to have. They are no fun.

14:05 When we got home the neighbor passed by to update us on the state of the Emperor. He hasn’t been seen for weeks. Granted he’s not likely to leave his palace but he hasn’t been spotted in the windows either.

16:40 I’ve stayed home. There is not much out there to do. My parents went with the neighbor.

18:30 We had dinner in the grand hall. Apparently the Emperor’s absence is a common topic at the moment. I am starting to worry myself if I’m quite honest.

22:10 Watched a scary show with my parents. It’s difficult to understand what’s happening at times but that doesn’t make it less scary. They seemed to enjoy it at least.


Diary entry 848.

Strange occurrence on an otherwise regular day.

10:30 I woke up, brushed my teeth, did my hair and went with a slightly different style than usual, hoping someone would notice. I changed clothes and went out for breakfast with the family in the grand hall.

11:30 Yesterday I missed them so today I left the door open so I can see the cleaners arrive when they come and I won’t have to rely on my very functional hearing.

13:30 Lunch time, I’ve worked some more on my art while I waited for time to pass.

15:20 My parents came home for a bit and allowed me to have some sweets. Surprisingly they actually stayed with me until dinner time.

18:30 We went back to the grand hall for dinner. The emperor has not been seen yet. Maybe he’s resting. I’m sure it’s not easy to oversee an entire system.

22:10 That same show as yesterday came on so we watched it together. However in the middle it was interrupted by an emergency broadcast. There wasn’t any imagery nor any subtitles so I’ve no idea what was said. Whatever it was, it seemed to upset my parents, they looked concerned yet.. Relieved. It’s hard to describe. They quickly send me to bed.

I’m sure they’ll tell me what that was tomorrow.


Diary entry 849.
This isn’t real. I am fairly certain this is a horrible nightmare.
I will try to write what I saw. I’m fearful.

10:30 I woke up to a cold breeze. I walked over to brush my teeth, make up my hair and change clothes. I found it strange that I couldn’t feel my parents walk around, for a moment I assumed they were off to a neighbor again. Until I stepped out of my room.

They were there, by the window, hanging from the ceiling. There was an empty noose next to them.
I haven’t looked at them since.
12:00 I’ve been sobbing and crying. It’s not just my parents. I haven’t found a single living person. I think it’s everyone.
I’ve looked out the window in the hallway. And I see more people hanging in the distance.
I don’t believe this is real.

13:40 I went to an empty apartment on the top floor. I don’t have to see anyone here. I don’t want to see anyone else.

14:44 I felt the emergency bells ringing, it was a deep rumble to my skin which I’ve only felt during tests, I stepped out on the balcony to see what was going on, hoping there would be an answer but there he was. The Emperor. And at least a hundred noblemen all slowly marching out the palace. I screamed hoping for something to happen. Nothing. They kept walking. Nobody even bat an eye. I thought the Emperor would save us. Just like he had done with so many before us. I screamed and begged.
It’s hard to write while I’m shaking.
He stopped moving in the middle of the plaza. I thought he finally heard my screams but he kneeled and looked up. His mouth moved but it was too far for me to read what he said before he burst into this red mass. I couldn’t move. My body forced me to watch as he erupted into a swarm of tendrils reaching for the ground while he grew into something horrific. The noblemen kept walking and collapsed into him, vanishing into the mass. Last thing I saw before could take control and run was the red mass growing and pulsating.

16:12 I haven't quite calmed down but I’ve at least managed to calm my breathing. This doesn’t feel real.
I don’t understand what is happening. Or if it even is. The Emperor would never let this happen. This would never happen.
We’ve always been happy. I feel dizzy. There is a hole in my mind I cannot fill. It doesn’t make sense. Was it yesterday’s broadcast? What was even said? I wish I could fucking hear.
It’s cold here.
This must be a nightmare. It’s the only thing that makes sense. I know what they’re like, they’re just like this. They can be the worst reality while feeling completely real.
This is the worst reality.
My parents would never leave me like this, I know they wouldn’t. And the Emperor, it cannot be real. That must be it. I need to wake up.
I have to wake up. I have to see mom and dad.

This videotape can be found on Hyx only.

Text ⁠
What is happiness?

Is it your dirty workplace?
Is it your filthy house?

Is it your crippling need for a therapist because you realised the universe is completely stacked against you and you will likely suffer the same fate as millions of others as the pressure of your worthless life becomes to much for the imagination of the mind leading to eventual damnination?


No!


Happiness is the one who sends you money!
Happiness is the one who created your job!
Happiness is the one who protects you!
Happiness is the Emperor!
And if you work hard enough,
You will be personally invited to live in his golden city!

Happiness is Empra!

Empra is happiness!

lore.title: Etern
lore.intro: Etern was home to a scientific lab where biological experiments took place. Many new lifeforms were created here among which are the famous Baboon Hawks.
